title: GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src: a skill pack so the agent stops writing last decade's web
friendlyTitle: A Chrome project gives coding agents current web advice
summary: This was the top repository on GitHub Trending today, with 799 stars in the day and about 2,700 overall. It is the source for Modern Web Guidance, a set of skills that put current browser guidance into a coding agent. Chrome, Edge, Mozilla, and MDN steward it. Code is Apache 2.0. The guides are CC BY 4.0. Install the published package with npx modern-web-guidance@latest install. Usage telemetry is on unless you set DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1.
friendlySummary: This was the most popular repository on GitHub today, with 799 new stars and about 2,700 in total. It holds the source for Modern Web Guidance, a pack of skills that teach a coding agent current browser practice. Chrome, Edge, Mozilla, and MDN look after it. The code is Apache 2.0. You install the published package, not this source folder, with one command. Usage tracking is on unless you turn it off.
whyItMatters: A coding agent often reaches for an old pattern because that is what its training data contains. This package gives it a current guide, and a scan for legacy patterns, instead of a heavy polyfill. You can try a search without installing. Their own evals, dated 6 November, show large gains on a fixed task set. Those are their measurements, not an independent audit. The trending repository is the source. The command above installs the package.
